scope: Offline functional-path qualification; no hardware calls, mutations or new control claimed.

ms.finding: Both calls reside in the same unwind-bounded function 82BBA0..82BD4E. 82BC1A invokes 771C00 with bool1; success sets local r15b. The routine performs an object operation at offset 0x214 and polls bit0. Its completion and timeout branches join at 82BD1B, which tests r15b then 82BD29 invokes 771C00 with bool0 before returning. The controller4 request is scoped to this internal operation; an external caller cannot hold it beyond that return through this path. This does not establish absence of other controls.
ms.next_requirement: A different externally callable request with an independent owned lifetime is required; tracing callers of82BBA0 cannot turn this bounded operation into a lasting hold.

native_contract.set_20801818: 8 bytes: u16 snoop value +0, u8 snoop scale +2, u16 no-snoop value +4, u8 no-snoop scale +6. Setter masks value 10 bits, scale 3 bits; no range validation in selected routine.
native_contract.request_8a254: snoop value bits10:1; snoop scale13:11; forced bit14=1; no-snoop value24:15; no-snoop scale27:25; forced bit28=1; bit0 trigger=1 and polled. Remaining retained bits follow read/modify/write mask 0xf0004001, combined with forced 0x10004001.
native_contract.get_20801817: reads 8a24c and projects snoop value9:0 scale12:10; no-snoop value23:14 scale26:24. Public output excludes status bits13 and27 and trigger-source bits. Error is suppressed by outer handler.
native_contract.relation: Shifting request fields and forced bits right by one matches the status field layout exactly; official NVIDIA GA102 published LAST_MSG_SENT uses the same status layout including requirement bits13 and27. This homologous mapping does not prove current register names, each SET reflected as latest message, requirement meaning, or ability to deassert.
native_contract.units: Pinned NVIDIA public API header gives no units or permitted scale semantics. Prior primary Linux source L1.2 threshold encoding uses scales0..5 for 1,32,1024,32768,1048576,33554432 ns; it is analogous PCIe encoding, not proof of this NVIDIA API. Scales6..7 are not rejected by selected setter; semantic validity is unestablished.
native_contract.ownership: No separate owned handle or release operation exists in public SET packet; setter issues a message trigger and returns after bit clears or timeout. Duration and replacement semantics beyond that event are not established.

zero_request_example.conclusion: Even with all four public values zero, the packed request differs from the captured all-zero raw baseline. Public GET omits these additional bits, so equality of its four fields cannot establish equality of the request.

primary_semantics.scope: Independent PCIe LTR example on Intel I210, not a binding of NVIDIA proprietary registers.
primary_semantics.paraphrase: With a requirement asserted, zero latency requests best service. Clearing the requirement denotes no latency requirement. Device-specific scale choices must not be generalized to this NVIDIA interface.

ltr.next_requirement: Bind the current NVIDIA request/status semantics and distinguish an actual reflected SET from unrelated last-message updates. No claim that unknown reset/replay behavior is a prerequisite to all other functionality.

other_scopes: ASPM and alternate NVDEC controller17 remain separately unqualified. Recovery, Undo and profile replay remain deferred. No new hardware trial was run.

vat_profiler.scope: Pinned 617.42 offline decoder audit only; no GPU operations or mutations.
findings: Current public header calls feature VAT without expanding it; profiler control bits11:10 encode ignore0, disable1 (0x400), enable2 (0x800), release3 (0xc00). B0CC0301 request packet is 12 bytes (globalStatus, controlMask, statusMask); B0CC0302 release is 4-byte controlMask. Documented request lifetime is tied to B2CC profiler object or explicit release.

Pinned Windows request handler 436730 decodes exactly five two-bit fields through 9:8; at 43688A it shifts input8 and masks3, decodes last field, then immediately calls 42EA10. It neither decodes VAT bits11:10 nor forwards them. Manager 42E305 restricts active request to 0x3ff.
Status translator 84DFA0..84E0F3 rewrites only bits0..9, leaving output status bits11:10 unchanged from caller input. They are not a VAT result and can mislead if zero initialized.

Release handler 435F80 checks five fields through mask0x300, then forwards to 42E830; VAT release bits do not reach manager. There is no selected VAT callback, current VAT capability probe or independent readback on this pinned request path. Behavior of other binaries is not inferred.

Descriptor E5C490 binds B0CC0301 size12 to wrapper 175B70 (+178), and B0CC0302 size4 to wrapper 175B80 (+180). For profiler HAL selector2, initializer 16F5CB1..CF4 assigns +178=436730 and +180=435F80; other HAL selectors can use distinct methods and are not covered by the real-handler findings.

elpg_enable_admission.scope: Offline static 617.42, no hardware or product mutation; source observations are not a universal driver guarantee.

findings.membership: Factory zeroes 0x1960 bytes. 3057e8 initializes support bitmap 0x3ffff7; 3057f2..81a invokes 736db0 only for its set bits, all below 22. 752430 adds only when 7383f0 confirms index <22 and currently supported. Three direct calls to removal helper 752480 at 739de9, 739f84, 73a0ff precede their respective support bit clears; removal clears the index in all four masks. These paths maintain membership subset of currently supported indices. Exhaustiveness of all support and membership writers is not established by this artifact.
findings.callback: 73a480 zero-count reason0 branch logs and calls +50 even if count was zero. 17e1580 selects 7377f0 if third descriptor word +10 equals 2, else 92d80 returns 0x56. 7377f0 resolves another object and, depending on its +48 low nibble and group+1958, calls e49a0 with callback 7345b0 and argument 0x258 or sets a bit in resolved+40. Thus callback is not generally equivalent to leaving all state unchanged on a zero mask. Descriptor selection for a specific runtime and e49a0 semantics are not established here.
findings.decision: Documented membership construction/update preserves selected members within supported IDs, and queued callback is policy-gated reevaluation consistent with ENABLE. However A801 type3 group support does not disclose the parallel object capability or reason bit: admission needs a qualified getter for GPU+2550 +f10 and, if active, +fc8 bit2 and +f24 semantics, or another source-proven constraint establishing the operation cannot affect an independently held request.
findings.deferred_followup: 7345b0 checks group+1958 then calls 305b00 and clears the queued flag. 305b00 iterates all supported members; 73a1f0 requires full reason mask +110 zero and state +114 nonzero before transition helpers 739620/73a5a0 and clears +114. If group+e3 set, 737b80 independently checks +11c zero and +120 before its own transition. This is a policy-gated all-supported reevaluation, not an unconditional reason0 count decrement; exact lower helper effects are not resolved. The third selector descriptor is cast from owner (fallback class 34a6d6) at 17e1f3b..f8f; its word +10 selects callback, but actual runtime value is not bound.
findings.parallel_object: Feature6 group case 42b784 requires GPU+2550+12c0, checks group0/1/3 masks and independently tests 7ec4e0(GPU+2550): +f10 >=2 and odd. If true, ENABLE/final release also calls 7ec3f0 with reason2, clears +fc8 bit2 and +f24 byte, and invokes object+130 method with state0 if resulting +fc8 is zero. A801 type3 reads the group object at +12c0 and cannot by itself exclude the parallel +f10 branch; it is not an alternative mutually exclusive group path. Current support reads do not establish +f10 or +fc8 values.

getter.entry: count=1, 16-byte entry type=12, index=0, attribute=3; flags at entry+6, value uint32 at entry+8
getter.binding: 4f3c94..b6 indexes jump table 4f40a4 with type-1; entry 12 reaches 4f3f5e; 4f3f82 calls 7ec550 with GPU+2550. Handler case attribute3 copies GPU+2550+f10 into entry+8. For attribute !=1, +28c and +fce must each be nonzero or valid flag remains clear; invalid means unknown.
getter.interpretation: When valid, (value < 2 or (value & 1)==0) makes 7ec4e0 false and excludes parallel +fc8 branch for this read state. Value >=2 and odd means branch active, not proof bit2 state.
getter.attribute6: Helper returns 1 << GPU+2550+f20 when byte +f24 equals 1, otherwise 0; not +fc8 reason bitmap.

getter.outline: On same selected device use existing A801 transport/geometry; send zero-initialized 0x404 bytes with count=1 and <HHH at offset4 set (12,0,3). Verify entry valid bit and preserved routing/opaque bytes as existing typed readers. If valid report uint32 value and predicate; do not interpret invalid as zero. No request executed.
getter.limit: Direct caller scan for 7ec4e0 finds only feature6 callback; direct reference scan identifies this typed capability getter but does not prove absence of indirect reason bitmap getters. If capability active, current binding does not expose +fc8 reason2 or establish +f24 lifecycle semantics.

findings: GPU initializer 11A350 obtains classID 0x112230 into GPU+0x2550. Public g_eng_desc_nvoc.h names that class Lpwr. Its creator 17AE010 invokes method initializer 17AD4C0 and property initializer 17AC190.

The 7EC060 initializer sets Lpwr+F10=3 and calls 16AAD0 with the literal RMPowerFeature (public nvrm_registry.h identifies this name). On successful read it extracts bits25:24: value1 clears F10 and F14 and +28C; if value0 and +28D nonzero it clears F10 and +28C; on failed read with +28D nonzero it clears F10/F14 and +28C. Remaining branches retain initial F10=3.

For source-bound chip HAL ordinals41..45, 17AD29D..2D5 and 337..33A initialize +28C and +28D to0; +130=6190, a three-byte success stub, per 17AD4C0 branch. This does not establish that later state mutations are harmless: 7EC3F0 still clears +FC8 bit2 and writes +F24=0. Other ordinals are not covered.

7EC6E0 may clear selected +F10 bits based on a graphics-object-derived maximum and per-entry configuration. Both 7EC060 initialization and 7EC6E0 filter are called only when +28C is nonzero on the observed normal caller path. For GB41..45, the factory initially zeroes the object and the generated property initializes +28C=0, so the normal initial path skips both routines. The earlier inference that F10=3 necessarily follows on this path was incorrect. Absence of later +28C writers or indirect initializer entry has not been proven; an unavailable getter remains insufficient as a current-state invariant.

+FC8 is a bitmask set and cleared by reason index in 7EC330/7EC3F0; +F24 is set or cleared respectively. Exact named feature and any authoritative owner semantics are unresolved. Nearby LpwrDtdPg strings are not sufficient to expand DTD or to identify these fields.

7EC6E0 derives a maximum from graphics +9C0 and 3B52C0 (which uses the +D40 virtual and 378D80 fallback); for each F10 bit it checks byte +D02[index]. If +F1C is nonzero, it substitutes low byte of the maximum for index0 and low byte of F1C for later indices. It clears the bit when the byte is zero or exceeds the maximum, then clears the entire mask unless it is odd and at least2. No complete public getter for these exact current inputs is established.

captured_read.interpretation: Entry unavailable is unknown, not zero and not evidence that the parallel branch is inactive. Normal construction observations do not establish current state.

findings.descriptors: The sorted A7/A8 range e69fb0..e6a110 ends A70F, A7D7, A801 then B201; no A802 in this range. A separate E802 descriptor e6add0 points 4f4100, flags 0x44 and size 0x404.
findings.setter: E802 4f4100 dispatches 16-byte entries; type3 checks controller support then calls 7388e0. That function jump table 738dbc admits attributes 3a, 3b, 4c. 3a constructs [value,0], 3b [0,value] and both call 738200; 4c follows a different guarded route. Existing A801 type3 GET supports 3a/3b/4c but exact correspondence remains unproven.
findings.conversion: For each nonzero u32 x, 738200 computes q=floor(uint64(x)*DWORD(LPWR+1318)/1000), takes low32(q), and replaces zero low32 with 1. Zero x passes as zero, but both zero rejected 0x1f. LPWR+1318 selected at 772de5 from LPWR+1314 when source+655 set, otherwise floor(DWORD(source+e28)/1000). Source units and admissible range remain unbound.
findings.dispatch: 738200 requires controller row+f1 and GPU+23b0+63e then calls 73acc0. This copies controller index and 16-byte control payload into firmware request 02 03 04, via 353ee0. Zero other field effect is not established. GET correspondence, endpoint behavior, units, admissible range, and exact readback contract remain unresolved.
findings.receiver_boundary: 73acc0 constructs size 0x24, header 02 03 04, index DWORD at +10, parameter block 16 bytes at +14, and sends through GPU+23b0+1038 -> 353ee0. Header low bits 2 select non-callback path; 354104..143 forwards through transport object vtable+30. Reviewed host construction and transport do not implement or reveal zero-peer behavior. Existing older-driver pmu-firmware-packaging-lead.json explicitly says PMU payload not identified; no matching receiver/protocol definition was found in bounded local source. Establish receiver behavior from corresponding 617.42 firmware or authoritative protocol before assuming zero ignores or overwrites peer.

findings: A801 type3 at 4F3CFE requires LPWR group object+12C0 and supported controller, then dispatches 738410. Jump-table index attr-6 maps 3A?73851D, 3B?738546, 4C?73856C.

3A/3B call 738130 and return first/second result respectively. It zeroes a two-word temporary, invokes group+98, then returns floor(raw*1000 / Lpwr+1318) for each 32-bit raw input. It ignores provider return status and has no local scale-zero guard. Thus the outer availability bit alone does not establish provider success.
4C directly calls the same provider and returns raw first; unlike 738130, its branch checks and propagates provider failure.

For chip HAL41..45 17E191D..937 selects group+98=B8FB80. Given controller hardware ID group+0xF0+0x108*index, B8FB80 rejects ID=0xFF; otherwise reads 32-bit words at 0x8F7100+4*ID and 0x8F7180+4*ID. Source establishes addresses for that family and pinned binary, not capability on a given adapter.

7388E0 setter jump table maps 3A?738B1F and 3B?738B88, each passing selected input and zero peer to 738200; 4C?738BAE passes raw first input and zero peer to 73ACC0. 738200 computes nonzero input as max(1, low32(floor(input*factor/1000))), preserving zero input as zero; rejects a pair that is all zero. Therefore scaled GET(SET(x)) generally differs from x due to truncation and min1, even if endpoint writes exactly converted raw.

No units for the public attributes or scale factor were established. An independent source trace found factor initialization from Lpwr+1314 or another clock-derived source; neither an exact current factor nor peer-zero endpoint semantics is yet established. Do not infer an exact safe set/readback or paired-field preservation merely from these branches.

7729FF obtains GPU+23B0 and 772DE5..E0C sets Lpwr+1318 to Lpwr+1314 when object+655 nonzero, otherwise floor(object+E28/1000). 11A1F0 binds GPU+23B0 to classID F3D722, identified in public generated source as Pmu.

A801 type3 4C returns raw first provider value R; 3A returns G=floor(1000*R/F), F=Lpwr+1318, assuming positive F and successful provider. If R>0 and G>0, integer F lies in floor(1000R/(G+1))+1 through floor(1000R/G). The factor is determined only if this interval is a singleton; repeated stable independent reads are needed. This is a mathematical inference, not a direct getter or proof the factor stays fixed during a SET.

The GB group provider B8FB80 issues full32 reads of 0x8F7100+4*hardware-ID and 0x8F7180+4*ID without masking. This proves driver read width, not native writable-field width or valid SET range. No exact matching register definition was found in checked public swref.

Pinned binary contains RMLpwrGrIdleThresholdUs and related literals, but a producer-to-attribute mapping was not established in this audit. Units therefore remain unknown. Nor is the firmware RPC zero-peer or actual-write mask semantics established.

The complete type3 attribute jump table 738834/7387F4 maps 3A to scaled first, 3B to scaled second, 4C to raw first. No other table case directly invokes the same group+98 two-word provider. The other cases use metadata or alternate performance paths; no source-qualified raw-second getter is identified.

GB group+98 provider B8FB80 reads hardware ID byte at group+F0+0x108*controller index, rejects 0xff, and reads 0x8F7100+4*ID and 0x8F7180+4*ID. 736DB0 initially sets the first per-controller byte (hardware ID) to 0xff even for controller0. The later producer and current typed ID getter remain unbound.

Controller index0 does not imply hardware ID0. No raw second-register address is qualified for the current adapter without the actual ID; do not match candidate values or sweep offsets. An exact ID producer/current getter or direct raw-second getter is the missing read-only join.

live_threshold_candidate.decision: Real live setter candidate, not a shipped control. Current scale is not uniquely determined, units are not source-qualified, and matching firmware receiver semantics for a zero peer are absent. No SET or guessed-register read was executed. This does not establish that the setter is write-suppressed or ineffective.
